newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Senate passes rail sale bill unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Australian Senate passes rail sale bill unchanged.

text.p: The Australian government's legislation for the sale of its rail operator Australian National (AN) was passed unchanged in the upper house of parliament, the Senate, late on Monday night.
The government needs two additional votes to pass any legislation in the non-government dominated Senate. The AN sale bill was passed with the support of Independents Brian Harradine and Mal Colston.
The Australian Democrats minor party said on Monday it would support the bill with certain amendments, but the proposals did not win the support needed for inclusion in the legislation.
The government late last year announced its intention to sell AN through a trade sale, which analysts expect to raise up to about A$600 million.
In May, Finance Minister John Fahey said the government had drawn up a shortlist of about 12 companies interested in AN or some of its assets from more than 50 expressions of interest.
The government last week said final bids for the rail operator were expected by mid-July.
AN operates freight services and workshops in South Australia and Tasmania, in addition to three interstate passenger services.
